Only 6 of 51 jurisdictions are free-and-deterministic today — NY, CO, CT, FL, OR, TX (all verified by live query 2026-08-28); ~12% of states, and California and Delaware are NOT among them, so the spec's HQ-state CRITICAL rule cannot stand as written.

The failure mode is real and named: Polimorphic, Inc. (DE C-corp, NYC HQ, VC-backed govtech AI) has NO New York DOS registration in NY's current open dataset, but IS registered in Colorado (20241401282, 'Noncompliant') and Connecticut ('Active — annual report past due') and has two SEC Form Ds (CIK 0001880550, inc_state DE) — the current spec would fire a false CRITICAL on a legitimate vendor.

SEC EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index, free, declared User-Agent required — 403 without one) is the single best existence check for the modal pitch profile: every VC-backed startup's Form D names its incorporation state, giving federal corroboration of Delaware incorporation without touching Delaware.

Delaware itself can never be automated: its free ICIS search's terms prohibit 'automated tools in any form' and 'mining data'; there is no API or bulk data; official status costs $10/entity — so 'no registration found' must never fire from a Delaware non-search, and the tool should emit a deep link + $10-status note instead.

For govtech vendors, customer-state foreign registrations often exist before HQ-state ones — so run the six-state open-data sweep in parallel on every evaluation (six free GET calls; any hit proves legal existence), rather than searching only the HQ state.

Most state portals actively defeat automated agents (verified today): CAPTCHAs in WY/ME/LA/SC/NE, hard 403/402 bot-blocks in GA/PA/IL/IA/KS/MS/MI/MO/MT/UT/NH/HI/TN/AR/OK/NV/OH, and JS empty shells in CA/WA/VA/AZ/ID/ND/NM/VT/IN/DC — an 'LLM web search of the SoS' will silently fail across most of the country.

Three states contractually prohibit automated searching even though search is free (DE, ME, NC verified) — the tool should honor these by policy and say so on its methodology page; NC bulk is paid-subscription only.

OpenCorporates is not a viable free backbone: paid tiers start at £2,250/yr for only 500 calls/month, the public site is now CAPTCHA-gated even for reading, ToS licenses website use for 'personal use only', free share-alike keys are limited to journalists/NGOs/academics, and 'government departments... are not Permitted Users' — any use needs a negotiated public-benefit agreement in writing.

Commercial KYB pricing is uniformly unpublished as of Aug 2026: Middesk and Baselayer are sales-quoted (no public prices), Cobalt Intelligence's site 403s all automated access (pricing unverifiable), and SOS-api.com's domain no longer resolves — budget planning must treat per-lookup costs ($1–$10 reported) as unverified.

Required rule change: 'no registration found' may fire as CRITICAL only after a deterministic source (Tier-A dataset or EDGAR) successfully returned a definitive empty result for a state where the vendor affirmatively claims incorporation/registration, or on affirmative negative evidence (revoked/dissolved); registry unreachable/paid/CAPTCHA states get a coverage-limited manual-check card with the state's official deep link — and silent errors must surface as coverage-limited, never 'not found.'

Benign compliance lapses ('Noncompliant', 'annual report past due') are common at young legitimate startups (both of Polimorphic's registrations show one) — style them as informational, not red-alarm.

Name-matching needs SPV discipline: the Texas Comptroller file contains eight 'Augment Collective, LLC Series Anthropic PBC N' investment SPVs alongside the real Anthropic, PBC (TX SOS file 0805470362) — flag SERIES/SPV/FUND patterns as non-identity matches.

Free federal corroboration lanes verified: GLEIF LEI API (free, no auth; empty for startups), SAM.gov Entity API (free but 10 requests/DAY without a federal role — corroboration only), IRS Pub 78/EO BMF monthly bulk for nonprofit vendors.

v1 can ship with zero paid dependencies (EDGAR + six-state sweep + Florida SFTP mirror + 50-state deep-link directory from llcuniversity.com); a paid KYB fallback would cost roughly $0.15–$1.75 per evaluation (uncertain estimate) firing on ~15–35% of evals, with a $10 hard ceiling (Delaware official status) — and its absence must never produce a harsher output than 'coverage limited.'

Socrata mechanics verified: use both $q= full-text and upper(col) LIKE queries, and register free app tokens per domain (unthrottled with token per dev.socrata.com); Florida's lane is a nightly SFTP mirror (sftp.floridados.gov, Public/PubAccess1845!), not a query API.
